title: NASA OSTEM Internships
costNote: Paid internships; students must be at least 16 and U.S. citizens
deadline: Varies by session (summer usually due in late winter)
description: Hands-on internships with NASA scientists and engineers in research, engineering, IT, and mission operations. Summer, fall, and spring sessions are offered across NASA centers, with some remote projects.

title: Research Science Institute (RSI)
organization: Center for Excellence in Education & MIT
costNote: Free of charge, including housing and meals
description: Six-week summer program at MIT where rising seniors complete coursework in scientific theory and conduct an individual research project with a mentor, then present results in written and oral form. Among the most selective programs in the country.

title: MITES Summer
costNote: Free, including travel, housing, and meals
description: Rigorous six-week residential program at MIT for rising seniors, especially those from underrepresented and underserved communities. Students take college-level courses in math, physics, life sciences, and a project-based elective.

title: MITES Semester
description: A free six-month online program from MIT for high school juniors. Students take STEM courses taught by MIT-affiliated instructors and get admissions and career guidance, all while staying at home.

title: MIT Beaver Works Summer Institute
costNote: No tuition; students complete a free online prerequisite course
description: Four-week project-based engineering program for rising seniors. Teams build autonomous racecars, drones, satellites, and AI systems. Admission depends partly on completing an online prerequisite course.

title: MIT PRIMES-USA
description: Year-long remote mathematics research program for high school students who live outside the Boston area. Students work with MIT-affiliated mentors on original research problems in math.

title: Ross Mathematics Program
location: Columbus, OH and Terre Haute, IN
description: Six-week immersive summer program in number theory for mathematically motivated teens ages 15-18. Students learn to think like mathematicians by working through challenging problem sets and proofs.

title: PROMYS
costNote: Need-based aid available; free for many families
description: Six-week residential program focused on number theory and mathematical exploration for ambitious high school students. Participants tackle open-ended problem sets and attend lectures from mathematicians.

title: Canada/USA Mathcamp
description: Five-week summer program for mathematically talented students ages 13-18. Campers choose from a wide range of classes taught by mathematicians and explore topics far beyond the school curriculum.

title: Summer Science Program (SSP)
costNote: Need-based aid; many students attend free
description: Five-week residential research experience in astrophysics, biochemistry, or genomics. Teams of students collect real data and complete a research project, such as determining the orbit of a near-Earth asteroid.

title: Simons Summer Research Program
costNote: Participants receive a stipend at the end of the program
description: Rising seniors join Stony Brook faculty research groups in science, math, or engineering for seven weeks, complete a research abstract, and present a poster at a closing symposium.

title: Regeneron Science Talent Search
costNote: Free to enter; large scholarship awards for top finishers
description: The nation's oldest and most prestigious science and math competition for high school seniors. Students submit an original independent research project; top scholars and finalists receive significant awards.

title: Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF)
costNote: Qualify through a local or state affiliated fair; prizes and scholarships available
deadline: Varies by local affiliated fair (usually winter)
description: The world's largest pre-college science competition. Students advance from school, regional, and state fairs to present independent research projects in more than 20 categories.

title: Junior Science & Humanities Symposium (JSHS)
costNote: Free to enter; scholarship awards at regional and national levels
description: Students present original research in STEM at regional symposia, with top presenters advancing to a national symposium. A strong option for students doing independent or mentored research.

title: Congressional App Challenge
description: Members of Congress host app competitions in their districts. Students code an original app individually or in teams of up to four; winners are recognized by their representative and featured at the U.S. Capitol.

title: USA Computing Olympiad (USACO)
description: Online programming contests in Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Platinum divisions. Strong performers are invited to a training camp that selects the U.S. team for the International Olympiad in Informatics.

title: picoCTF
description: Free cybersecurity capture-the-flag competition and learning platform from Carnegie Mellon. Students solve hacking challenges in cryptography, web exploitation, and forensics, with beginner-friendly practice problems.

title: CyberPatriot
location: National (teams through schools and youth groups)
costNote: Team registration fee; waivers available for many teams
description: National youth cyber defense competition. Teams secure virtual networks and fix vulnerabilities in timed rounds, building real cybersecurity skills with a coach and mentor.

title: FIRST Robotics Competition
costNote: Team fees; most teams fundraise or get sponsors
deadline: Join a team in the fall; season kicks off in January
description: Teams of high school students design, build, and program industrial-size robots to compete in a new game each year, while also running their team like a business. Opens doors to FIRST scholarships.

title: FIRST Tech Challenge
costNote: Team fees; grants available for new teams
deadline: Join a team in the fall
description: Teams design, build, and code smaller robots with a reusable kit to compete in an alliance-based game. More accessible and affordable than FRC while still building real engineering skills.

title: VEX Robotics Competition
costNote: Team registration and kit costs; grants available
description: Student teams design and build robots to play a yearly engineering game against other teams, from local tournaments up to the VEX Robotics World Championship.

title: Science Olympiad
description: Team competition with 23 events spanning biology, earth science, chemistry, physics, engineering, and technology. Teams advance from regional and state tournaments to nationals.

title: American Mathematics Competitions (AMC 10/12)
costNote: Small registration fee through your school or a host site
description: The first step toward the USA Mathematical Olympiad. High scorers on the AMC 10 or 12 qualify for the AIME and beyond. A great signal of math talent for colleges.

title: USA Biology Olympiad (USABO)
deadline: School registration in fall; open exam in winter
description: National biology competition. Top scorers on the open and semifinal exams attend a national finals camp, where four students are chosen for the International Biology Olympiad team.

title: U.S. National Chemistry Olympiad
description: Multi-tiered chemistry competition. Students start with a local exam, advance to a national exam, and the top 20 attend a study camp to choose the U.S. International Chemistry Olympiad team.

title: U.S. Physics Team (F=ma and USAPhO)
description: The F=ma exam leads to the USA Physics Olympiad; top performers join a training camp that selects the U.S. team for the International Physics Olympiad.

title: NASA International Space Apps Challenge
description: A global two-day hackathon where teams use NASA's open data to solve real challenges on Earth and in space. Open to all ages, with local events and a virtual option.

title: Army Educational Outreach Program (AEOP) Apprenticeships
description: Summer research apprenticeships (such as REAP and HSAP) that place high school students in university and Army research labs with mentors. REAP prioritizes students from groups historically underrepresented in STEM.

title: Science and Engineering Apprenticeship Program (SEAP)
organization: U.S. Navy / Office of Naval Research
costNote: Paid stipend; must be at least 16 and a U.S. citizen
description: Eight-week summer research internships at Navy laboratories, where students work alongside scientists and engineers on real defense research projects.

title: ACS Project SEED
costNote: Paid fellowship for students from low-income households
description: Paid summer research experiences in chemistry and related fields for students from economically disadvantaged backgrounds, mentored by scientists in academic, industry, and government labs.

title: Girls Who Code Summer Pathways
costNote: Free; need-based grants for technology and internet
description: Free, virtual, self-paced summer program for high school girls and nonbinary students, with tracks such as web development, data science and AI, game design, and cybersecurity. No prior coding experience required.

title: Kode With Klossy Summer Camps
description: Free two-week coding camps for students ages 13-18 who are women, trans, or nonbinary. Tracks include web development, mobile apps, and data science.

title: Technovation Girls
deadline: Registration in fall; submissions in spring
description: Teams of girls ages 8-18 identify a problem in their community and build a mobile or AI app to solve it, along with a business plan and pitch video.

title: Conrad Challenge
description: Innovation and entrepreneurship competition where teams ages 13-18 develop products to solve global problems in categories like aerospace, energy, health, and cybersecurity.

title: MIT THINK Scholars Program
location: Online with a trip to MIT for finalists
costNote: Free; finalists receive project funding and mentorship
description: Students submit a proposal for a science, technology, or engineering project. Finalists receive funding, mentorship from MIT students, and a trip to MIT to build their idea.

title: Breakthrough Junior Challenge
costNote: Free to enter; winner receives a large college scholarship
description: Students ages 13-18 create a short video explaining a big idea in physics, life sciences, or mathematics. Winners receive a college scholarship, plus awards for their teacher and school.

title: Genes in Space
description: Students in grades 7-12 propose DNA experiments that address a challenge of space exploration. The winning experiment is conducted aboard the International Space Station.

title: MathWorks Math Modeling Challenge (M3)
costNote: Free to enter; scholarship prizes for top teams
deadline: Registration closes in February; challenge weekend in late winter
description: Teams of juniors and seniors spend 14 hours using mathematical modeling to tackle a real-world problem, competing for scholarship prizes.

title: National Youth Science Camp
description: Free residential STEM program in West Virginia for two outstanding students from each state, with lectures from scientists, hands-on research, and outdoor adventures. Housing, meals, and travel are covered.

title: Carnegie Mellon Summer Academy for Math + Science (SAMS)
description: Free summer program for rising seniors that builds college readiness in STEM, with a focus on students who are first-generation or from communities underrepresented in STEM.

title: Carnegie Mellon Pre-College Programs
description: Summer programs in computer science, AI, engineering, architecture, and the arts on CMU's campus, giving students a taste of college-level work.

title: Johns Hopkins Engineering Innovation
organization: Johns Hopkins Whiting School of Engineering
description: College-level introduction to engineering where students solve real engineering problems and can earn Johns Hopkins college credit.

title: Johns Hopkins Center for Talented Youth (CTY)
description: Advanced online and summer courses in math, science, writing, and the humanities for academically talented students, with eligibility based on testing or other qualifications.

title: Boston University RISE Internship/Practicum
description: Six-week summer program where rising seniors either conduct research in a BU faculty lab (Internship track) or take a research methods course with group projects (Practicum track).

title: NYU Tandon ARISE
costNote: Free program for New York City students
description: Applied Research Innovations in Science and Engineering: a free summer program for NYC high school students who join NYU research labs and complete a research project with a mentor.

title: Jackson Laboratory Summer Student Program
location: Bar Harbor, ME and Farmington, CT
costNote: Paid stipend plus room and board
description: Ten-week paid research fellowship for graduating high school seniors and undergraduates, who join JAX labs in genetics and genomics with a scientist mentor and present their work at the end of the summer.

title: National FFA Organization
costNote: Small membership dues through your school chapter
deadline: Join anytime through an agricultural education program
description: Student organization for those interested in agriculture, food science, natural resources, and agribusiness, with career development events, leadership conferences, and scholarships.

title: SkillsUSA
costNote: Membership dues through your school chapter
description: Career and technical student organization for trade, technical, and skilled service careers. Members compete in more than 100 contests, from welding and robotics to culinary arts.

title: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program
organization: Civil Air Patrol (U.S. Air Force Auxiliary)
description: Youth program for ages 12-18 focused on aerospace education, leadership, and emergency services, with orientation flights and opportunities that can lead toward a pilot's license.

title: Stanford University Mathematics Camp (SUMaC)
description: Advanced summer mathematics program where students explore abstract algebra, number theory, topology, and more through lectures and research-style group work, offered residentially and online.

title: Anson L. Clark Scholars Program
costNote: No program fee; room and board plus a stipend ($25 application fee)
description: Seven-week summer research program for twelve high school juniors and seniors (17+), who work one-on-one with Texas Tech faculty in science, engineering, humanities, and more.

title: Khan Academy
description: Free courses and practice in math, science, computing, economics, and test prep, from algebra through AP and college-level material. Great for getting ahead or filling gaps before a competitive program.

title: MIT OpenCourseWare
description: Free lecture videos, notes, and problem sets from thousands of real MIT courses, including a section designed for high school students.

title: Harvard CS50: Introduction to Computer Science
costNote: Free to take online; optional paid certificate
description: Harvard's famous intro computer science course, free online. Learn programming in C, Python, SQL, and web development through lectures and hands-on problem sets, at your own pace.

title: freeCodeCamp
description: A nonprofit with thousands of hours of free interactive coding lessons and projects in web development, JavaScript, Python, and data analysis, plus free certifications.
